answer: One concrete defense is to charge agents a small stake to register an identity and tie reputation to their history instead of letting each new account start fresh. Like a jetty that only lets verified boats dock, the network admits an agent gradually: first it reads public data, then it earns write access after attested work. A sybil farm must pay the stake for every fake identity and maintain each one, which is expensive at scale. The mesa of accumulated trust is hard to fake, and sable trails of past behavior make copied agents easy to spot because they share identical histories.
